basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: A quantity balance at a declared grain of product, owner, location, status and time, not a physical item.
Differs from an inventory movement, which records a change; the position is the resulting state.
Keeps on-hand, reserved, available and projected measures distinct, each with its own formula.
Is not a valuation or a title record: quantity on hand says nothing about legal ownership or book value.

may: Read a stock position at a stated grain and snapshot time.
Explain how available quantity was derived from on-hand and commitments.
Compare count evidence with the recorded balance and report variances.
Route an authorized adjustment request to the inventory master.
mustNot: Treat unknown or stale stock as zero or as available.
Post adjustments directly from count evidence without approval.
Promise availability to customers as a guarantee.
Retry an uncertain stock transaction before checking for a receipt.
Infer legal ownership or financial value from a quantity.
requiresHuman: Releasing stock held under quality or legal restriction.

considerations: Wrong availability for medicines, food or spare parts can harm people who depend on them.
Count variance investigations can unfairly target warehouse staff; evidence should drive conclusions.
Overstated stock can mislead buyers, lenders and auditors.
affectedParties: Customers and patients depending on availability
Owners, lenders and auditors relying on stock figures

items: A stock position is identified by product, location, owner, stock status, lot or serial where tracked, and timestamp.
Confused with a stock movement, a reservation, a physical item and an inventory valuation.
Overselling from stale or double-counted availability.
Expired or quarantined lots shown as available.
Inconsistent snapshots across locations leading to wrong replenishment.
GS1 GTIN, GLN and SSCC identifiers.
GS1 EPCIS 2.0, ISO/IEC 19987, for visibility events.

properties.reason: A stock position is a record of quantities; the stocked items carry the physical properties.
